# FastDog Networks

> FastDog puts a website that runs on your own server on the public internet over HTTPS, without opening ports. You add your address, add two DNS records, run a small agent on your server, and check a live status page. Human docs: /docs/ on this site.

## Concepts

- Edge: FastDog's public server. It answers for your address, serves HTTPS with an automatic certificate, and forwards each request to your server.
- Agent: a small program on your server. It opens one outbound connection to the edge and keeps it open, so no inbound ports or firewall changes are needed and your server's IP stays private.
- Origin: where your app listens on that server, for example http://127.0.0.1:3000.
- Portal: the signed-in customer site where setup happens.

## Setup

1. Add the website address in the portal (a subdomain such as app.example.com; root domains need ALIAS/ANAME/CNAME flattening).
2. Add two DNS records at the domain's DNS provider:
   - CNAME on the address, pointing at the attach target the portal shows. It routes visitors to FastDog.
   - TXT on _fastdog-challenge.<address> with the value the portal shows. It proves ownership.
   - On Cloudflare set Proxy status to "DNS only" (grey cloud). Orange cloud hides the record from the check and blocks the certificate.
3. Connect the server: the portal returns a one-time connect command for Linux (recommended) or Docker. It contains a private key: never print it to logs, commits or chats. A new command replaces the old key.
4. Check the Status page: Live / Not live, last checked, certificate expiry, agent connected, origin answering, 24h requests, p50 latency, bot-check counts (shadow mode, nothing blocked), and a Test it button.

## Connect token API (for AI assistants)

The user creates a prompt on the portal's Server page. It contains a connect token (prefix fdct_) that works for one hostname, can only read that hostname's connection status and get its connect command once, expires after one hour, and is revocable. Send it only as a header: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Tokens in URLs are rejected.

- GET {portal}/api/connect/v1/hostname -> {hostname, scope, expires_at, command_issued, agent: {connected, last_seen, origin_reachable, origin_checked_at}}
- POST {portal}/api/connect/v1/command with JSON {"origin": "http://127.0.0.1:<port>", "platform": "linux" | "docker"} -> {hostname, platform, origin, command}. Single use per token (409 token_used after). Origins must be local or private addresses with a port (400 invalid_origin otherwise).
- Errors: 401 unauthorized (missing, expired or revoked token), 429 rate_limited (honour Retry-After).

Suggested flow: ask the user which port the app uses; call the command endpoint once; have the user run the command on the server (it uses sudo; the user types their own password); poll the hostname endpoint every 10 seconds until agent.connected is true; then open https://<hostname>/ to confirm.

## API keys (scripts and assistants)

Signed-in users with any paid plan create API keys on the portal's API keys page. A key (prefix fdak_) is shown once, stored only as a hash, belongs to one account, can be limited to exact hostnames, expires after 30 days by default (90 at most), and can be revoked at any time. A password change or a suspended account ends every key. Send it only as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`; keys in URLs, bodies or cookies are rejected. A key can never create another key.

Scopes (a key holds one or more):
- `hostnames:create`: add a hostname and check its DNS. Counts against the plan's hostname limit.
- `status:read`: read live status.
- `connect`: get a connect command (replaces the current server connection; at most 3 per hostname per day with keys).
Removing a hostname is not possible with a key; it is done in the portal.

- POST {portal}/api/v1/hostnames with JSON {"hostname": "app.example.com"} -> 201 {hostname, status, dns: {cname, txt}} (`hostnames:create`)
- GET {portal}/api/v1/hostnames/<hostname> -> {hostname, status, dns?, agent?} (`status:read` or `hostnames:create`)
- POST {portal}/api/v1/hostnames/<hostname>/verify -> {hostname, status, verified, checks} (`hostnames:create`)
- GET {portal}/api/v1/hostnames/<hostname>/status -> {live, reasons, checked_at, agent, cert, traffic, verdict} (`status:read`; verdict counts are shadow only)
- POST {portal}/api/v1/hostnames/<hostname>/connect with JSON {"origin": "http://127.0.0.1:<port>", "platform": "linux" | "docker"} -> {command} (`connect`)
- Errors: 401 unauthorized (missing, expired or revoked key), 403 forbidden (scope or hostname not allowed by this key), 404 hostname_not_found, 409 hostname_limit_reached / not_active, 429 rate_limited (60 requests a minute per key; honour Retry-After).

## Troubleshooting

- Records not seen: wait a few minutes; check the TXT name starts with _fastdog-challenge. and the provider did not append the domain twice.
- Agent connected but origin not answering: start the app or fix the origin address. Inside Docker, 127.0.0.1 is the container; use host.docker.internal on Docker Desktop.
- No certificate yet: it is issued on the first visit once DNS points at FastDog.
